test_cases.scenario: Unauthenticated user cannot access the Sprints page
test_cases.steps:
1. Open a browser with no active session.
2. Navigate directly to the Sprints page URL.
test_cases.expected: The user is redirected to the login page. No sprint data is visible.

test_cases.scenario: Authenticated user with view permission can access the Sprints page
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in with a valid account.
2. Navigate to Planning > Sprints from the main menu.
test_cases.expected: The Sprints page loads. The eyebrow reads 'Planning', the title reads 'Sprints', and the subtitle reads 'Manage sprint periods, their status, and lifecycle within each financial year.'

test_cases.scenario: Add Sprint button is visible for users with create permission
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user with sprint create permission.
2. Navigate to the Sprints page.
test_cases.expected: The 'Add Sprint' button is visible in the page header.

test_cases.scenario: Generate Sprints button is visible only for users with generate permission
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user with generate sprint permission.
2. Navigate to the Sprints page.
test_cases.expected: The 'Generate Sprints' button is visible in the header. A user without this permission does not see it.

test_cases.scenario: Edit, Toggle Active, and Set Active actions are hidden for read-only users
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a read-only user.
2. Navigate to the Sprints page.
3. Observe row actions.
test_cases.expected: No Edit, Toggle Active, or Set Active action buttons appear on any row.

test_cases.scenario: Lock / Unlock action is only visible for users with the close sprint permission
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user with can_close_sprint permission.
2. Navigate to the Sprints page.
3. Observe row actions.
test_cases.expected: The 'Lock / Unlock' action is visible. A user without can_close_sprint does not see this action.

test_cases.scenario: Delete action is only visible for users with delete permission
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user with sprint delete permission.
2. Navigate to the Sprints page.
test_cases.expected: The Delete action button is visible. A user without delete permission does not see it.

test_cases.scenario: Detail page is accessible by clicking a sprint row
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the Sprints page.
2. Click on any sprint row (not an action button).
test_cases.expected: The user is navigated to the sprint's detail page showing the full sprint information and capacity table.

test_cases.scenario: Rebuild Capacity button on the detail page is only visible for users with change permission
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to a sprint detail page as a user with change permission.
test_cases.expected: The 'Rebuild Capacity' button is visible. A read-only user does not see it.

test_cases.scenario: Breadcrumb on the sprints list page reflects Planning > Sprints
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the Sprints page.
test_cases.expected: The breadcrumb trail correctly reflects the Planning > Sprints path.

test_cases.scenario: Sprint records load and display in the table on page open
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the Sprints page.
test_cases.expected: All existing sprint records are displayed in the table without errors.

test_cases.scenario: Table displays the correct columns on desktop
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the Sprints page on a desktop viewport.
2. Observe column headers.
test_cases.expected: Columns appear in order: Name, Financial Year, Code, Start Date, End Date, Month, Status, Closed, Active, Created.

test_cases.scenario: Search field filters sprints by name
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the Sprints page.
2. Type part of a sprint name into the search field.
test_cases.expected: The table updates to show only sprints whose names match the search term.

test_cases.scenario: Search with no matching results shows the empty state
test_cases.steps: 1. Type a term that matches no sprint name.
test_cases.expected: The table shows 'No sprints found.' with no data rows.

test_cases.scenario: Clearing the search field restores the full list
test_cases.steps:
1. Apply a search term.
2. Clear the search field.
test_cases.expected: The full list of sprints is restored.

test_cases.scenario: Sprint Status filter shows only sprints with the selected status
test_cases.steps: 1. Click the Status filter and select a specific sprint status.
test_cases.expected: The table shows only sprints matching the selected status. Others are hidden.

test_cases.scenario: Financial Year filter shows only sprints belonging to that financial year
test_cases.steps: 1. Click the Financial Year filter and select a specific financial year.
test_cases.expected: The table shows only sprints belonging to the selected financial year.

test_cases.scenario: Is Active filter set to Active shows only active sprints
test_cases.steps: 1. Set the Active filter to 'Active'.
test_cases.expected: Only sprints where is_active is true are shown.

test_cases.scenario: Is Active filter set to Inactive shows only inactive sprints
test_cases.steps: 1. Set the Active filter to 'Inactive'.
test_cases.expected: Only sprints where is_active is false are shown.

test_cases.scenario: All four filters can be combined to narrow results
test_cases.steps:
1. Type a search term.
2. Select a Sprint Status.
3. Select a Financial Year.
4. Set Is Active to 'Active'.
test_cases.expected: The table shows only sprints that satisfy all four criteria simultaneously.

test_cases.scenario: Active filter chips appear for each applied filter
test_cases.steps: 1. Apply the Status filter and the Financial Year filter.
test_cases.expected: Active filter chips appear for each applied filter. Clicking a chip removes that filter.

test_cases.scenario: Table can be sorted by Name ascending and descending
test_cases.steps:
1. Click the Name column header.
2. Click it again.
test_cases.expected: Sprints sort alphabetically by name, then reverse.

test_cases.scenario: Table can be sorted by Start Date and End Date
test_cases.steps:
1. Click Start Date header, then End Date header.
2. Click each again.
test_cases.expected: Sprints sort by the selected date column in ascending then descending order.

test_cases.scenario: Table can be sorted by Month and Created
test_cases.steps:
1. Click the Month header.
2. Click the Created header.
test_cases.expected: Sprints sort by month and by creation date respectively.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking a sprint row navigates to the sprint detail page
test_cases.steps: 1. Click anywhere on a sprint row (not on an action button).
test_cases.expected: The browser navigates to the sprint's detail page. The page title updates to the sprint's name.

test_cases.scenario: Pagination controls work when many sprints exist
test_cases.steps:
1. Ensure more than 25 sprints exist.
2. Use the next and previous page controls.
test_cases.expected: Page navigation works correctly. Each page shows the expected subset of records.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking Generate Sprints opens the generate drawer
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the Sprints page (as a user with generate permission).
2. Click the 'Generate Sprints' button.
test_cases.expected: The Generate Sprints drawer slides open. The drawer title reads 'Generate Sprints' with eyebrow 'Engine'.

test_cases.scenario: Generate drawer contains the Financial Year field and a hint
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Generate Sprints drawer.
2. Observe the form.
test_cases.expected: The drawer contains a required Financial Year dropdown and a hint reading 'Sprints are auto-generated based on the configured sprint duration. The selected financial year must have no existing sprints.'

test_cases.scenario: Selecting a financial year with no existing sprints and generating creates all sprints for that year
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Generate Sprints drawer.
2. Select a financial year that has no existing sprints.
3. Click 'Generate Sprints'.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes or shows a success state. All sprints for the selected financial year are created automatically based on the configured sprint duration. The sprint list refreshes to show the generated sprints.

test_cases.scenario: Financial Year is required in the generate drawer
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Generate Sprints drawer.
2. Leave the Financial Year field unselected.
3. Click 'Generate Sprints'.
test_cases.expected: A validation error appears indicating the Financial Year is required. No sprints are generated.

test_cases.scenario: Selecting a financial year that already has sprints shows an error
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Generate Sprints drawer.
2. Select a financial year that already has sprints.
3. Click 'Generate Sprints'.
test_cases.expected: An error message is shown indicating the selected financial year already has sprints and generation cannot proceed.

test_cases.scenario: Generate Sprints button is not visible for users without generate permission
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user without the generate sprint permission.
2. Navigate to the Sprints page.
test_cases.expected: The 'Generate Sprints' button is not visible in the page header.

test_cases.scenario: Closing the generate drawer without submitting makes no changes
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Generate Sprints drawer.
2. Select a financial year.
3. Click Cancel.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. No sprints are generated.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking Add Sprint opens the create drawer
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the Sprints page.
2. Click the 'Add Sprint' button.
test_cases.expected: The create drawer slides open with a blank form. The drawer title reads 'Create Sprint'.

test_cases.scenario: Create drawer contains all expected form fields
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Add Sprint drawer.
2. Observe the form fields.
test_cases.expected: The form contains: Financial Year (required), Sprint Number (required), Name (optional — auto-generated if blank), Start Date (required), End Date (required), Note (optional).

test_cases.scenario: A sprint is created successfully with all required fields
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Add Sprint drawer.
2. Select a Financial Year.
3. Enter a Sprint Number.
4. Set a Start Date and End Date.
5. Click 'Create Sprint'.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. A success toast appears. The new sprint appears in the table with correct financial year, code, dates, and status.

test_cases.scenario: Sprint Name is auto-generated when left blank
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Add Sprint drawer.
2. Fill in Financial Year, Sprint Number, Start Date, and End Date.
3. Leave the Name field blank.
4. Click 'Create Sprint'.
test_cases.expected: The sprint is created with an auto-generated name. The Name field in the table is populated automatically.

test_cases.scenario: Custom sprint name is used when provided
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Add Sprint drawer.
2. Enter a custom name in the Name field.
3. Fill in all required fields and submit.
test_cases.expected: The sprint is created with the custom name shown in the table.

test_cases.scenario: Financial Year is required — validation error shown when empty
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Add Sprint drawer.
2. Leave Financial Year unselected.
3. Fill in other fields and click 'Create Sprint'.
test_cases.expected: A validation error appears under Financial Year. The sprint is not created.

test_cases.scenario: Sprint Number is required — validation error shown when empty
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Add Sprint drawer.
2. Leave Sprint Number empty.
3. Fill in other required fields and submit.
test_cases.expected: A validation error appears under Sprint Number. The sprint is not created.

test_cases.scenario: Start Date is required — validation error shown when empty
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Add Sprint drawer.
2. Leave Start Date empty.
3. Fill in other required fields and submit.
test_cases.expected: A validation error appears under Start Date. The sprint is not created.

test_cases.scenario: End Date is required — validation error shown when empty
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Add Sprint drawer.
2. Leave End Date empty.
3. Fill in other required fields and submit.
test_cases.expected: A validation error appears under End Date. The sprint is not created.

test_cases.scenario: End Date set before Start Date shows a validation error
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Add Sprint drawer.
2. Set a Start Date.
3. Set End Date to a date before the Start Date.
4. Click 'Create Sprint'.
test_cases.expected: A validation error is shown indicating the End Date must be on or after the Start Date.

test_cases.scenario: Note is optional and the sprint can be created without it
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Add Sprint drawer.
2. Fill in all required fields.
3. Leave Note blank.
4. Submit.
test_cases.expected: The sprint is created without a note.

test_cases.scenario: Closing the create drawer without submitting discards entered data
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Add Sprint drawer.
2. Fill in some fields.
3. Click Cancel.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. No sprint is created. The form is blank when reopened.

test_cases.scenario: Success toast appears and drawer closes after creating a sprint
test_cases.steps: 1. Create a sprint with all required fields and submit.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes automatically. A success toast appears confirming the sprint was created.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking a sprint row navigates to the detail page
test_cases.steps: 1. Click on any sprint row on the Sprints page.
test_cases.expected: The browser navigates to the sprint detail page. The page title shows the sprint's name.

test_cases.scenario: Detail page left panel shows all sprint information fields
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to any sprint detail page.
2. Observe the left info panel.
test_cases.expected: The info panel shows: Sprint Number, Name, Financial Year, Code (code style), Start Date, End Date, Month, Status, Closed, Note, Created, and Created by.

test_cases.scenario: Sprint Timer panel shows a progress bar for the current sprint period
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the detail page of a sprint that is currently in progress.
2. Observe the Sprint Timer panel.
test_cases.expected: A progress bar is visible showing how much of the sprint period has elapsed. Meta text below the bar shows relevant timing information.

test_cases.scenario: Sprint Timer progress bar reflects correct completion percentage
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the detail page of a sprint that started several days ago and has several days remaining.
test_cases.expected: The progress bar fills proportionally to the percentage of the sprint period that has elapsed.

test_cases.scenario: Detail page right panel shows the Capacity table
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to any sprint detail page.
2. Observe the Capacity section.
test_cases.expected: A Capacity table is visible showing columns: Member, Team, Location, Working Days, Holidays, Leaves, Net Capacity.

test_cases.scenario: Capacity table shows correct net capacity for each member
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to a sprint detail page.
2. Review the Net Capacity column for listed members.
test_cases.expected: Net Capacity for each member reflects working days minus holidays and leaves for the sprint period.

test_cases.scenario: Capacity table search filters by member name
test_cases.steps: 1. On the sprint detail page, type a member name into the Capacity search field.
test_cases.expected: The capacity table filters to show only the matching member(s).

test_cases.scenario: Capacity table Team filter shows only members from the selected team
test_cases.steps: 1. On the sprint detail page, select a team from the Team filter in the Capacity section.
test_cases.expected: The capacity table updates to show only members belonging to the selected team.

test_cases.scenario: Capacity table shows empty state when no members are assigned
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to a sprint detail page for a sprint with no team members assigned.
test_cases.expected: The capacity table shows 'No capacity data found for this sprint.'

test_cases.scenario: Forecast button on the detail page opens the forecast view
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to a sprint detail page.
2. Click the 'Forecast' button.
test_cases.expected: The forecast view or panel opens for the selected sprint.

test_cases.scenario: Actuals button on the detail page opens the actuals view
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to a sprint detail page.
2. Click the 'Actuals' button.
test_cases.expected: The actuals view or panel opens for the selected sprint.

test_cases.scenario: Rebuild Capacity button regenerates capacity data for the sprint
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to a sprint detail page (as a user with change permission).
2. Click 'Rebuild Capacity'.
test_cases.expected: The capacity data is recalculated. The Capacity table refreshes with updated values reflecting current member assignments, holidays, and leaves.

test_cases.scenario: Breadcrumb on the detail page links back to the Sprints list
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to a sprint detail page.
2. Click the Sprints breadcrumb link.
test_cases.expected: The user is navigated back to the Sprints list page.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking the Edit action opens the edit drawer pre-populated
test_cases.steps: 1. Click the Edit action button on a sprint row.
test_cases.expected: The edit drawer opens with the sprint's current Name, Start Date, End Date, and Note pre-filled.

test_cases.scenario: Financial Year and Sprint Number are not editable after creation
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer for any sprint.
2. Observe the available fields.
test_cases.expected: The edit drawer shows only Name, Start Date, End Date, and Note. Financial Year and Sprint Number are not present — they cannot be changed after creation.

test_cases.scenario: Name is required in edit mode — validation error shown when cleared
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer for a sprint.
2. Clear the Name field.
3. Click 'Save changes'.
test_cases.expected: A validation error appears under Name. The change is not saved.

test_cases.scenario: Name can be updated successfully
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer.
2. Change the Name to a new value.
3. Click 'Save changes'.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. A success toast appears. The updated name is reflected in the table.

test_cases.scenario: Start Date can be updated successfully
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer.
2. Change Start Date to a valid new date.
3. Click 'Save changes'.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. The updated Start Date is reflected in the table.

test_cases.scenario: End Date can be updated successfully
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer.
2. Change End Date to a valid new date.
3. Click 'Save changes'.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. The updated End Date is reflected in the table.

test_cases.scenario: Clearing Start Date shows a validation error
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer.
2. Clear Start Date.
3. Click 'Save changes'.
test_cases.expected: An inline validation error appears. The change is not saved.

test_cases.scenario: Setting End Date before Start Date in edit mode shows a validation error
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer.
2. Set End Date to a date before Start Date.
3. Click 'Save changes'.
test_cases.expected: A validation error is shown. The change is not saved.

test_cases.scenario: Note can be added or updated in edit mode
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer for a sprint with no note.
2. Enter a note.
3. Save.
test_cases.expected: The note is saved and visible on the sprint detail page.

test_cases.scenario: Closing the edit drawer without saving discards changes
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer.
2. Change the Name.
3. Click Cancel.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. The sprint retains its original name.

test_cases.scenario: Success toast appears after saving sprint edits
test_cases.steps: 1. Make a valid change in the edit drawer and save.
test_cases.expected: A success toast appears confirming the sprint was updated.

test_cases.scenario: Toggle Active on an active sprint shows a deactivate confirmation modal
test_cases.steps:
1. Find an active sprint.
2. Click the Toggle Active action.
test_cases.expected: A deactivation confirmation modal appears.

test_cases.scenario: Toggle Active on an inactive sprint shows an activate confirmation modal
test_cases.steps:
1. Find an inactive sprint.
2. Click the Toggle Active action.
test_cases.expected: An activation confirmation modal appears.

test_cases.scenario: Confirming deactivation marks the sprint as inactive
test_cases.steps:
1. Click Toggle Active on an active sprint.
2. Confirm deactivation.
test_cases.expected: The modal closes. The sprint's Active column changes to inactive. A success toast confirms the change.

test_cases.scenario: Confirming activation marks the sprint as active
test_cases.steps:
1. Click Toggle Active on an inactive sprint.
2. Confirm activation.
test_cases.expected: The modal closes. The sprint's Active column changes to active. A success toast confirms the change.

test_cases.scenario: Cancelling the activate/deactivate modal leaves the sprint unchanged
test_cases.steps:
1. Click Toggle Active on any sprint.
2. Click Cancel in the modal.
test_cases.expected: The modal closes. The sprint's active state is unchanged.

test_cases.scenario: Set Active action is visible for sprints not currently in progress
test_cases.steps:
1. Find a sprint whose Status is not 'In Progress'.
2. Observe the row actions.
test_cases.expected: The 'Set Active' action button is visible for that sprint.

test_cases.scenario: Set Active action is hidden for sprints already in progress
test_cases.steps:
1. Find a sprint whose Status is 'In Progress'.
2. Observe the row actions.
test_cases.expected: The 'Set Active' action button is not visible for the in-progress sprint.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking Set Active marks the sprint as the current in-progress sprint
test_cases.steps:
1. Click 'Set Active' on a sprint that is not currently in progress.
2. Confirm if prompted.
test_cases.expected: The sprint's Status updates to 'In Progress'. A success toast confirms the change. The Set Active action disappears for this sprint.

test_cases.scenario: Only one sprint per financial year can be in progress at a time
test_cases.steps:
1. Note which sprint is currently in progress.
2. Click Set Active on a different sprint in the same financial year.
test_cases.expected: The new sprint becomes 'In Progress'. The previously in-progress sprint's status is updated. Only one sprint is in progress at any given time.

test_cases.scenario: The in-progress sprint is reflected in the sprint pill in the page header
test_cases.steps:
1. Set a sprint as active (In Progress).
2. Observe the sprint pill/indicator in the application header.
test_cases.expected: The sprint pill in the header updates to show the name and remaining time of the newly activated sprint.

test_cases.scenario: Lock / Unlock action is visible for users with the close sprint permission
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user with can_close_sprint permission.
2. Navigate to the Sprints page.
test_cases.expected: A 'Lock / Unlock' action button (lock icon) is visible on sprint rows.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking Lock / Unlock on an open sprint locks it
test_cases.steps:
1. Find a sprint where is_closed is false.
2. Click the Lock / Unlock action.
3. Confirm if prompted.
test_cases.expected: The sprint's Closed column updates to show locked/closed. A success toast confirms the sprint is now locked.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking Lock / Unlock on a locked sprint unlocks it
test_cases.steps:
1. Find a sprint where is_closed is true.
2. Click the Lock / Unlock action.
3. Confirm if prompted.
test_cases.expected: The sprint's Closed column updates to show unlocked/open. A success toast confirms the sprint is now unlocked.

test_cases.scenario: Lock / Unlock action is not visible for users without the close permission
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user with change permission but WITHOUT can_close_sprint.
2. Navigate to the Sprints page.
test_cases.expected: The Lock / Unlock action is not shown on any sprint row.

test_cases.scenario: The Closed column in the table reflects the locked/unlocked state
test_cases.steps:
1. Lock a sprint.
2. Observe the Closed column for that sprint.
test_cases.expected: The Closed column shows a locked indicator. After unlocking, it shows an unlocked indicator.

test_cases.scenario: Locked sprint's closed state is visible on the sprint detail page
test_cases.steps:
1. Lock a sprint.
2. Navigate to the sprint detail page.
test_cases.expected: The Closed field in the info panel on the detail page shows the locked/closed state.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking Delete shows a confirmation modal
test_cases.steps: 1. Click the Delete action on a sprint row.
test_cases.expected: A delete confirmation modal appears referencing the selected sprint.

test_cases.scenario: Confirming deletion permanently removes the sprint
test_cases.steps:
1. Click Delete on a sprint.
2. Type the required confirmation text.
3. Click the confirm delete button.
test_cases.expected: The modal closes. The sprint is removed from the table. A success toast confirms the deletion.

test_cases.scenario: Delete confirm button is disabled until correct confirmation text is typed
test_cases.steps:
1. Click Delete on a sprint.
2. Leave the confirmation field empty or type incorrect text.
test_cases.expected: The confirm delete button remains disabled.

test_cases.scenario: Cancelling the delete modal keeps the sprint intact
test_cases.steps:
1. Click Delete on a sprint.
2. Click Cancel.
test_cases.expected: The modal closes. The sprint remains in the table.

test_cases.scenario: Delete confirmation modal warns the action is permanent
test_cases.steps:
1. Click Delete on any sprint.
2. Read the modal body text.
test_cases.expected: The modal warns that deletion is permanent and cannot be undone.

test_cases.scenario: Import button is visible on the Sprints page
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the Sprints page with manage permissions.
test_cases.expected: An Import button is visible in the page header.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking Import opens the import view
test_cases.steps: 1. Click the Import button.
test_cases.expected: The import view opens with options to download a sample file and upload a file.

test_cases.scenario: Sample import file can be downloaded
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the import view.
2. Click the sample file download link.
test_cases.expected: A CSV sample file is downloaded with the expected import columns.

test_cases.scenario: A valid CSV imports sprints successfully
test_cases.steps:
1. Prepare a valid CSV with financial_year, sprint_number, start_date, and end_date.
2. Upload it and confirm the import.
test_cases.expected: The import completes. A success message shows the count of records imported. The table shows the new sprints.

test_cases.scenario: Uploading an invalid file format is rejected
test_cases.steps: 1. Attempt to upload a .pdf or image file.
test_cases.expected: The import view rejects the file and shows an error message.

test_cases.scenario: Importing a row with an invalid financial year shows a row-level error
test_cases.steps:
1. Prepare a CSV with a financial_year value that does not exist in the system.
2. Import it.
test_cases.expected: The import reports an error for that row. The row is skipped.

test_cases.scenario: Importing a row where End Date is before Start Date shows a row-level error
test_cases.steps:
1. Prepare a CSV row where end_date is before start_date.
2. Import it.
test_cases.expected: A date validation error is reported for that row. The row is not imported.

test_cases.scenario: Table refreshes after a successful import
test_cases.steps:
1. Import a valid CSV.
2. Observe the table.
test_cases.expected: The sprint table refreshes and shows the newly imported sprints.

test_cases.scenario: Export button is visible on the Sprints page
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the Sprints page with manage permissions.
test_cases.expected: An Export button is visible in the page header.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking Export opens the export view
test_cases.steps: 1. Click the Export button.
test_cases.expected: The export configuration panel opens.

test_cases.scenario: Sprints can be exported and a file is downloaded
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the export view.
2. Configure and initiate the export.
test_cases.expected: A file is downloaded containing sprint data.

test_cases.scenario: Exported file contains expected columns
test_cases.steps:
1. Export all sprints.
2. Open the file.
test_cases.expected: The file includes: Name, Financial Year, Code, Start Date, End Date, Month, Status, Closed, Active at minimum.

test_cases.scenario: Export respects active Financial Year filter
test_cases.steps:
1. Filter by a specific financial year.
2. Export.
test_cases.expected: The exported file contains only sprints from the filtered financial year.

test_cases.scenario: Export view can be closed without exporting
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the export view.
2. Close without downloading.
test_cases.expected: The export view closes. No file is downloaded.

test_cases.scenario: All interactive elements on the Sprints page are keyboard accessible
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the Sprints page.
2. Use only Tab and Enter/Space to reach and activate all controls: filters, buttons, row actions.
test_cases.expected: Every interactive element is reachable and operable by keyboard.

test_cases.scenario: Full sprint creation can be completed via keyboard only
test_cases.steps:
1. Use keyboard to open the Add Sprint drawer.
2. Tab through Financial Year, Sprint Number, Name, Start Date, End Date.
3. Submit via keyboard.
test_cases.expected: A sprint is created successfully without using the mouse.

test_cases.scenario: Focus is trapped within open drawers
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Add Sprint drawer.
2. Press Tab repeatedly.
test_cases.expected: Focus cycles within the drawer and does not escape to the page behind.

test_cases.scenario: Delete confirmation modal is keyboard accessible
test_cases.steps:
1. Trigger the delete modal via keyboard.
2. Tab between Cancel and Confirm.
3. Activate via Enter.
test_cases.expected: Focus is managed inside the modal. Both buttons are keyboard reachable.

test_cases.scenario: Validation error messages are clear and descriptive
test_cases.steps:
1. Submit the create form with all required fields empty.
2. Read the error messages.
test_cases.expected: Each error clearly states what field is required or invalid.

test_cases.scenario: No internal error details are exposed to the user
test_cases.steps:
1. Trigger error conditions (invalid input, network errors).
2. Observe error messages.
test_cases.expected: Messages are user-friendly and do not expose stack traces, database errors, or server details.

test_cases.scenario: Session expiry prevents sprint actions
test_cases.steps:
1. Allow the session to expire.
2. Attempt to create or edit a sprint.
test_cases.expected: The user is redirected to login. No data is changed.

test_cases.scenario: Both sprints list page and detail page render correctly in dark theme
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the Sprints page and then to a detail page.
2. Toggle to dark theme.
test_cases.expected: All elements render correctly in dark mode — table, filters, drawers, capacity table, progress bar.

test_cases.scenario: Sprints page and detail page load within an acceptable time
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the Sprints page and then to a detail page.
test_cases.expected: Both pages and their data load within a reasonable time (typically under 3 seconds).

test_cases.scenario: All table columns are visible on desktop viewports
test_cases.steps: 1. Open the Sprints page on a desktop browser (viewport ≥ 1024px).
test_cases.expected: All columns are visible: Name, Financial Year, Code, Start Date, End Date, Month, Status, Closed, Active, Created.

test_cases.scenario: All four filters are displayed inline in the filter bar on desktop
test_cases.steps: 1. View the Sprints page on a desktop viewport.
test_cases.expected: Search, Sprint Status, Financial Year, and Is Active filters are shown horizontally in the filter bar above the table.

test_cases.scenario: Detail page shows left info panel and right capacity panel side by side on desktop
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to a sprint detail page on desktop.
test_cases.expected: The sprint information panel occupies the left column and the Capacity section occupies the wider right column.

test_cases.scenario: Forecast, Actuals, and Rebuild Capacity buttons are aligned in the detail page header on desktop
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to a sprint detail page on desktop.
test_cases.expected: Forecast, Actuals, and Rebuild Capacity buttons are aligned horizontally in the page header without overflow.

test_cases.scenario: Drawers open as a wide side panel on desktop
test_cases.steps: 1. Open the create drawer on a desktop browser.
test_cases.expected: The drawer opens at 900px width as a side panel. Financial Year, Sprint Number, Start Date, and End Date are shown in a two-column grid.

test_cases.scenario: Secondary columns are hidden on mobile viewports
test_cases.steps: 1. Open the Sprints page on a mobile viewport (≤ 767px).
test_cases.expected: Financial Year, Code, Start Date, End Date, Month, Closed, Active, and Created are hidden. Name and Status remain visible.

test_cases.scenario: Add Sprint drawer is usable on mobile
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Add Sprint drawer on a mobile device.
2. Fill in required fields.
3. Submit.
test_cases.expected: The drawer is fully functional on mobile. The sprint is created without layout issues.

test_cases.scenario: Start Date and End Date stack vertically in the create drawer on mobile
test_cases.steps: 1. Open the Add Sprint drawer on a mobile viewport.
test_cases.expected: Start Date and End Date are stacked vertically on small screens.

test_cases.scenario: Sprint detail page stacks info panel above capacity panel on mobile
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to a sprint detail page on a mobile viewport.
test_cases.expected: The info panel stacks above the Capacity section. Both sections are scrollable and fully readable.

test_cases.scenario: Capacity table secondary columns are hidden on mobile
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to a sprint detail page on a mobile viewport.
2. Observe the Capacity table.
test_cases.expected: Team, Location, Working Days, Holidays, and Leaves columns are hidden. Member and Net Capacity remain visible.

test_cases.scenario: Filters are accessible on mobile
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Sprints page on a mobile viewport.
2. Tap each filter dropdown.
test_cases.expected: All four filters (Search, Sprint Status, Financial Year, Is Active) are accessible and functional on mobile.

test_cases.scenario: Page header does not overflow on small mobile viewports
test_cases.steps: 1. Open the Sprints page on a 375px-wide viewport.
test_cases.expected: Title and action buttons do not overflow or overlap.

test_cases.scenario: Sprint capacity accounts for member leaves during the sprint period
test_cases.steps:
1. Record a leave for a member during a sprint period.
2. Navigate to the sprint detail page.
test_cases.expected: The member's Leaves column in the capacity table shows the correct leave days. Net Capacity is reduced accordingly.

test_cases.scenario: Sprint capacity accounts for public holidays during the sprint period
test_cases.steps:
1. Ensure a public holiday exists during a sprint period for a member's location.
2. Navigate to the sprint detail page.
test_cases.expected: The member's Holidays column shows the correct holiday count. Net Capacity reflects the reduction.

test_cases.scenario: Rebuild Capacity updates capacity after leave or holiday changes
test_cases.steps:
1. Add a leave for a member during a sprint.
2. Navigate to the sprint detail page.
3. Click 'Rebuild Capacity'.
test_cases.expected: The capacity table refreshes and reflects the updated leave days and net capacity.

test_cases.scenario: Sprints belong to a Financial Year and are filtered by it
test_cases.steps:
1. Create sprints for two different financial years.
2. On the Sprints page, filter by one financial year.
test_cases.expected: Only sprints belonging to the selected financial year are displayed.

test_cases.scenario: The active (in-progress) sprint is reflected in the sprint pill in the application header
test_cases.steps:
1. Set a sprint as active (In Progress).
2. Navigate to different pages of the application.
test_cases.expected: The sprint pill in the application header shows the name and end date of the in-progress sprint across all pages.

test_cases.scenario: Generating sprints for a financial year creates one sprint per configured duration period
test_cases.steps:
1. Open Generate Sprints.
2. Select a financial year with no existing sprints.
3. Generate.
test_cases.expected: The correct number of sprints is created to cover the full financial year duration, each with appropriate start and end dates based on the configured sprint length.

test_cases.scenario: Financial Year filter in the Sprints page shows only active financial years
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the Sprints page.
2. Click the Financial Year filter dropdown.
test_cases.expected: The Financial Year filter lists financial years configured in the system.

test_cases.scenario: Sprint code is unique and auto-generated from financial year and sprint number
test_cases.steps:
1. Create two sprints with different sprint numbers under the same financial year.
2. Compare their codes.
test_cases.expected: Each sprint has a unique auto-generated code that incorporates the financial year and sprint number.
